paragraphs: Yellow Duck Sweater dreamed it was waiting in a library, and the library was made of socks. The shelves were knitted, ribbed tubes stacked like bricks, and the books were socks rolled tight and stood up on their toes. The carpet was one enormous argyle. Nothing made a sound. The duck's feet landed without a click, which worried it, because in the simulator it had never once been quiet. It nudged a rolled sock with its head, and the sock unrolled across the floor like a long woolen page. Knitted into it was a small yellow duck, walking forward one stitch per step.

It followed the page down an aisle lit by lamps with sock shades. At the far end a giant microduck sat at a desk with its back turned, knitting. The duck froze with one foot raised, the way it had practiced for a hundred checkpoints, and the giant did not turn. It only held a long yellow thread out behind its chair without looking, and the thread ran along the carpet back to the hem of the duck's own sweater, which was a little shorter than before. The duck stood still and let the stitches count it. Behind it, the page kept growing across the carpet and ended in half an orange foot, not yet finished.

imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: The robot duck in its yellow duckling sweater stands in a hushed library where the tall shelves are knitted from thick ribbed socks and the books are socks rolled tight and standing on their toes, over a floor-wide argyle carpet. Panel 2: Close-up: the duck's orange feet step silently on the argyle carpet, and the duck tilts its head to look at its own quiet feet with its round camera eye wide. Panel 3: The duck nudges one rolled sock with its head and the sock unrolls across the carpet like a long woolen page with a tiny knitted yellow duck walking along it. Panel 4: The duck follows the unrolling woolen page down a long aisle lit by lamps with sock-shaped shades, the tiny knitted duck on the page always one step ahead. Panel 5: At the far end of the aisle a giant microduck sits at a desk with its back turned, knitting, while the duck stands frozen with one orange foot raised, and a long yellow thread trails from the giant's chair along the carpet. Panel 6: The duck stands very still beside the long woolen page, which ends in a half-knitted orange foot, while the yellow thread runs back to the hem of its sweater and the giant knits on in the background. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
